note.summary: Skiers and snowboarders share why they love Blue Mountain Resort, highlighting its runs, scenery, and community. It is an advertisement for Blue Mountain Resort.
note.hook: An aerial shot of a snowy mountain with ski slopes and ski lifts.
note.voiceover: I've been a season pass holder here for eight years, but I've been skiing here for 30 years. I love Blue Mountain because it has a lot of good runs, it has a lot of challenging runs, and it has a lot of runs that I'm capable of doing and having fun on. Love that all my friends work here at the mountain, and it's a beautiful place to come and ski and have fun. Amount of trails, diversity, and just the camaraderie and life-long friends here. I love the trails. Just love the scenery. It's a great place to snowboard. The snow is pretty much always great whenever we come out here. It's just pretty much perfect for me. The mountain, I love the quietness. I love the the people seem a lot more calmer on the mountain.

note.summary: This video ad celebrates 20 years of Jay Peak Championship Golf, highlighting the course's natural beauty, rugged landscape, and wild character.
note.hook: A logo appears celebrating 20 years of championship golf at Jay Peak.
note.voiceover: For twenty years, we've celebrated the kind of beauty that can't be manufactured. Fairways that flow with the landscape, navigating its elevation changes, natural contours, and the occasional chunk of stubborn granite. Greens are shared with the occasional fox or moose. Reminders everywhere that this place is better because it's a little wild. It's a beauty that's untamed, defined by character, not convention. Twenty years in, the course looks and plays better than ever. Come see it for yourself.
note.onscreen: CELEBRATING / 20 YEARS / OF CHAMPIONSHIP GOLF / 2006 - 2026 / JAY PEAK / VERMONT

note.summary: This video ad features the spa manager of Sundance Mountain Resort, highlighting the resort's natural beauty, spa services, and connection to nature.
note.hook: A warm, rustic interior with hanging lights and a stone fireplace.
note.voiceover: My name is Jonna Slade. I lead the spa and wellness teams at Sundance Mountain Resort. I first started at the spa in 2003. I worked there for nine years, moved away for nine years, and came back as a role in my role as manager. Simply spending time in nature is proven to provide health benefits and create a sense of overall well-being. From its beginnings, the spa at Sundance has sought to provide a healing space, grounded in ancient traditions, to bring balance and connection of mind and body through the power of nature. This might come through a warm stone massage, a morning yoga or meditation session, a body treatment or facial utilizing the healing properties of honey, mud, or gemstones. This connection to nature has the power to remind us all that we are all part of something bigger than ourselves. And there's really something so peaceful in that. We have a beautiful view of Timpanogos from our front door. When I leave each day after work, I look at this mountain and I feel the connection to nature and how lucky I am that I get to share it with others.
note.onscreen: sundance MOUNTAIN RESORT / DISCOVER THE PEOPLE / DISCOVER THE PEOPLE / JONNA SLADE / Spa Manager

note.summary: This video shows behind-the-scenes footage of workers replacing a ski lift cable at Bromont, explaining the complex process of splicing the new cable.
note.hook: A worker explains behind-the-scenes ski lift maintenance while workers handle equipment in the background.
note.voiceover: Derrière la scène qu'on ne voit jamais, aujourd'hui c'est une belle occasion, on procède au remplacement complet du câble de la remontée. Donc dans le cas de la remontée 2, c'est un câble qui a plus de 15 ans. On suit vraiment l'état de ces pièces maîtresses-là. Étape 1, on retire les chaises, après ça on amène la nouvelle bobine, on l'installe en place. C'est une bobine qui pèse 11,5 tonnes. On coupe le vieux câble et on le joint avec le nouveau. On tire tout doucement, on fait le tour de la remontée comme ça. Par la suite, c'est là que la magie opère, où est-ce qu'on va faire une épissure. Donc l'épissure c'est un processus pour joindre les deux bouts de câbles ensemble et en faire une boucle continue. Le câble est composé de torons, c'est de détouster tout ça sur 38 mètres de long pour rentrer dedans pour remplacer un bout de câble, parce que tu peux pas avoir un fil qui dépasse. C'est sûr que le changement de câble, il se fait en partenariat avec Doppelmayr, on a aussi un expert venu d'Europe pour faire les épissures avec nous.
note.onscreen: L'arrière scène, on le voit jamais, / une belle occasion. / Aujourd'hui, on procède au remplacement complet de la remontée. / SAMUEL / COORDINATEUR À L'ENTRETIEN INDUSTRIEL / RETIRE LES CHAISES. / APRÈS ÇA, ON AMÈNE LA BOBINE, ON L'INSTALLE EN PLACE. / C'EST UNE BOBINE QUI PÈSE 11,5 TONNES. / ON COUPE LE VIEUX CÂBLE / ET ON LE JOINT AVEC LE NOUVEAU. / ON TIRE TOUT DOUCEMENT / LE TOUR DE LA REMONTÉE / ÇA. PAR LA SUITE, LA MAGIE OPÈRE / OÙ EST-CE QU'ON / VA FAIRE UN ÉPISURE. / DONC L'ÉPISURE C'EST / UN PROCESSUS POUR / JOINTER LES 2 / BOUTS DE CÂBLES ENSEMBLE / ET D'EN FAIRE / UNE BOUCLE CONTINU

note.summary: This video ad promotes Brundage mountain resort, showcasing winter sports like skiing and snowboarding, as well as summer activities like mountain biking and outdoor concerts, emphasizing a deep connection with nature.
note.hook: An aerial shot of a snowy mountain peak and forested valley under a bright blue sky.
note.voiceover: It's hard to believe that a place like this exists, but in the idealized memories of those who lived before us, a place where nature reigned unspoiled and uncompromised. But for many of us today, unimaginable until you experience it for yourself. From her peaks, you can see the Western Rockies spread before you. And at her feet, McCall. Hugging the shining waters of the lake she feeds with her expansive banquet of snow. In the spring, summer and fall, previously unseen trails emerge like hidden treasures, revealing endless paths to nearly twenty thousand acres of mountain and backcountry. And whether your way of discovery is the tread of two tires or a pair of shoes, you can't help but feel the profound presence of nature in full beauty. And when she dresses in white and becomes the storied winter playground, you recall her reputation as having the best snow in Idaho. And nod your head after your first powder run. Skis or boards, groomed or backcountry, snowshoes or snowmobiles, from catching snowflakes to catching air. This is winter for all, in all its splendor. As the future unfolds, Brundage welcomes those who long to live the mountain life. Here, they'll find a community, neighbors embracing nature while enfolded within her arms. Where development honors the history and the future. And preservation takes precedence over growth. Creating a beautiful balance tuned to the mountain in harmony with the environment, welcoming those who never forget who was here first. This is
note.onscreen: THE MOUNTAIN FIRST / THE MOUNTAIN ALWAYS / BRUNDAGE
note.offer: Experience Brundage, the mountain first, the mountain always.
note.music: Inspiring and uplifting acoustic and orchestral music.

Someone wants to chase pow, someone wants groomer laps, and someone's already thinking about après. And yet, we're supposed to agree on just one mountain. Luckily, we don't have to, because with Epic Pass, we have five different mountains to choose from here in Colorado. So we can see what the snow's doing, how everyone's feeling, and figure it out from there. And with ski season right around the corner, now's the time to lock in your Epic Pass. Strong enough to snap a pine tree right in half. Meaner too. They say he buries people alive in their cabins while they're sleeping. Poor folks don't even know what hit them. They say his name literally translates to 'The Boy,' but he ain't no boy. I'm not sure if he's even a man. Something not of this world. They say... Are you guys talking about El Niño again? I told you, it's just a weather pattern. All it means is Monarch is going to get a ton of snow this year. So you're saying he controls the weather? No, no, I'm saying he is the weather. Pshh! That is one bad dude! [whistles] I'm not ready. I'm not ready. With a legendary winter on the horizon, you'll want to beat the storm and stake your claim before prices jump on Dec. 1st. Are you ready?

lp.t: Best Seattle Ski Resort Near Mt Rainier | Crystal Mountain

note.summary: This video ad for Crystal Mountain resort showcases stunning mountain scenery, wildlife, and summer activities like hiking and dining, inviting viewers to explore the mountain in the summer.
note.hook: A breathtaking timelapse of the sunrise over the Cascade mountain range.
note.voiceover: In the heart of the Cascade range, a warm breeze carries the sounds of summer. Crystal Mountain has finally shed its winter coat, and summer time is here at last. Trails have re-emerged, weaving merrily through the hills. Wildflowers paint the slopes with color. Streams wander through the old forests, and the clear waters of alpine lakes shimmer in the sunlight. Climbing out of the valley, Mount Rainier Gondola takes you all the way to the summit, where you can dine at the highest elevation restaurant in Washington. Fill your belly and feast your eyes. This place is ever green, except for the rugged peaks, the accent ridge lines of a mountain range that stretches as far as the eyes can see. But it all soars to Tacoma, inspiring awe in everyone. Long days of sunshine are here, but they won't last forever. It's time to get up and explore at Crystal Mountain.
note.onscreen: EXIT LEFT / 15 / CRYSTAL
note.offer: Get up and explore at Crystal Mountain.
note.music: Uplifting and cinematic orchestral music with a sense of wonder

note.summary: Skiers and snowboarders share why they love Blue Mountain Resort, highlighting its runs, scenery, and community. It is an advertisement for Blue Mountain Resort.

note.voiceover: I've been a season pass holder here for eight years, but I've been skiing here for 30 years. I love Blue Mountain because it has a lot of good runs, it has a lot of challenging runs, and it has a lot of runs that I'm capable of doing and having fun on. Love that all my friends work here at the mountain, and it's a beautiful place to come and ski and have fun. Amount of trails, diversity, and just the camaraderie and life-long friends here. I love the trails. Just love the scenery. It's a great place to snowboard. The snow is pretty much always great whenever we come out here. It's just pretty much perfect for me. The mountain, I love the quietness. I love the the people seem a lot more calmer on the mountain.

note.summary: This video ad tells the story of the "bootpackers" of Aspen Highlands Ski Patrol who spend 15 days climbing the Highland Bowl before it opens to create a discontinuity in the snowpack and prevent avalanches. It sells the unique experience of skiing the Highland Bowl.
note.hook: A snowy mountain ridge against a bright sky.
note.voiceover: This term, bootpacking, has become a term of accessing terrain. If you go to other mountains and they say, "Oh yeah, we've set a bootpack," it means they get off the chairlift and they hike up a a mound, a hill, a mountain, and they put their skis on and they ski down. That might be one of the biggest misconceptions of what bootpacking is.

note.summary: This video ad tells the story of Lucas Herbert, a content specialist at Arapahoe Basin, who overcame severe mental health struggles and suicidal ideation through his passion for skiing and the outdoors. The ad promotes Ikon Pass and includes a mental health crisis helpline message.
note.hook: A skier zips down a snowy mountain slope, capturing action footage with a camera.
note.voiceover: My name is Lucas Herbert. I'm the camera guy at A-Basin. One of the parts of my job that I really, really enjoy is the collaboration aspect. When you can coordinate on a shot and it's like, that's exactly what I was looking for, you can see the frames rolling through the camera as you're holding down the record button. And you can hear them screaming through the stoke of it. And you just know it's that special moment. There's no better feeling in the world. My job really consists of getting to go out and ski the best parts of the hill in the best conditions with some of the best talent. Crazy that this is where skiing has taken me. It feels so real sometimes. Fourteen-year-old me, my head would explode. The mountains are places for people to come together and heal. I think that's why I moved out to Colorado. You know, I really struggled with mental health growing up. I was dealing with so much depression and anxiety, very low self-esteem. There's a lot of feeling like I didn't fit in. The isolation was crushing. I was prescribed all kinds of different medications. I definitely started to abuse it a little bit because I wanted to forget about the really hard things that I was doing with in my life and it just spiraled from there. At that low point in my life, it was really hard for me to see what my future was going to look like. Emotionally, I was just I felt trapped and I didn't see a way out. I tried to take my own life. I ended up in an inpatient facility. I had a really h

lp.t: Colorado Ski Resorts on Epic Pass | Epic Season Pass

note.summary: A snowboarder shares her excitement for the upcoming ski season in Colorado, showcasing various snowboarding clips and highlighting the flexibility of having an Epic Pass.
note.hook: A person dances in a gondola, saying money buys a ski pass.
note.voiceover: Money doesn't buy happiness, but it does buy a ski pass. So if you're looking for me this winter, check the mountain. Hi, and welcome to another season of living, working, and running around in a ski town, and another season of trying to get a hundred days on the mountain. We are less than a month away from this being our reality, and so I'm so excited for a brand new season of exploring all of the Colorado ski resorts with my Epic Pass. And the best part about having a pass is that there isn't this pressure to have the best ski day ever every single day, because you can just try again tomorrow. And some of my favorite days aren't even the ones with the deepest snow. They're the random Tuesday morning first tracks, or stopping for a midday apress, or staying out in the park until last chair. And that's really the best part about being out on the mountain. You don't know which days are going to be your favorite until you get out there. So here is to day one, and day two, and eventually, because we are dedicated, day 100.

note.voiceover: I'm here at Deer Valley, UT and this season, Deer Valley is being added to the Ikon Base Pass. This means that all Ikon Pass Holders now have the opportunity to explore the largest ski resort expansion in North American history, which has been completed for this winter. That's 2,000 new acres of skiable terrain across 135 new trails and 16 new lifts, doubling the resort's size in the past three years to make it one of the largest ski resorts in North America. The finishing touch to this masterpiece of an expansion is the Hail Peak Express, right behind me, a new high-speed quad that will provide an additional 200 acres of skiable terrain across 7 new runs. With Deer Valley now on the Ikon Base Pass, all Ikon Pass users now have the opportunity to explore four resorts in Utah, making it the perfect way to chase that famous Utah powder. For Base Pass holders, that's an unlimited amount of days at Solitude, 5 days at Brighton, 5 days at Snowbird, and 3 days at Deer Valley. Make sure you make a reservation for Deer Valley with your Ikon Base Pass to let them know you're coming. The Ikon Pass is on sale for only a few more weeks, so go and grab your pass right now.
